brief: Goldman Sachs's weekly kickstart frames the period around "Competition for Capital": AI-driven demand for capital and rising fiscal borrowing have pushed up the cost of capital. Despite higher yields, nominal GDP growth and corporate earnings stay strong, supported by technology earnings and AI-related investment. Higher cost of capital and greater capital intensity in Technology have weighed on valuations, but compute demand is accelerating and outstripping supply; GS frames the key risk as whether earnings growth proves unsustainable, not valuations alone. Higher yields support a gradual increase in bond allocations, but resilient earnings keep GS constructive on equities, recommending staying invested while diversifying across sectors, countries and styles. For the week, global equities fell 0.5%, Europe down 1.9% and the US broadly flat; Health Care and Tech led sector gains (+1.6%, +0.9%); gold fell 0.2% as a hawkish Fed tempered momentum. GS raised EPS growth forecasts for the S&P 500 and MSCI EM. This week's calendar includes US durable goods, several Fed speakers, European PMIs and central bank decisions, and the Trump-Xi summit.
